title: Model Experiment Playbook: deterministic A/B scheduler, safety budgets, and auto-revert policies
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Goal: Deliver a pragmatic A/B testing framework for model versions that teams can use to run deterministic experiments, limit blast radius with configurable safety budgets, and automatically revert unsafe model variants. This playbook will include: an experiment scheduler with deterministic seedable splits, per-experiment safety budgets (max negative signal allowed), a sequence of statistical checks (early stop, bias and latency checks), an auto-revert mechanism tied to SLOs and safety signals, and UI/CLI primitives for operators to inspect and intervene.

Scope: Product-facing experiment primitives (API + Console flows) and the policy definitions for automated revert. Engineering will build the scheduler and signal evaluation pipeline; DX/Docs will publish a playbook and quickstart templates. Initial rollout will support text-generation endpoints and hosted/dedicated deployments.

Out-of-scope for MVP: cohort stratification UI, cross-region coordinated rollouts, and long-running drift detection (these are follow-ups).

Success metrics: 
- 90% of internal teams can run an A/B experiment with safety budget configured within 30 minutes.
- Auto-revert triggers correctly identify and revert variants with high-severity failures in >=95% of test incidents.
- Mean time to detect negative-signal crossing the safety budget < 10 minutes for high-sensitivity configs.

Risks & trade-offs: 
- Tight safety budgets increase false positives and may reduce meaningful exposure; include a cooldown window and human override.
- Deterministic splits require careful seeding to avoid correlated user groups causing biased results.
- Auto-revert must be conservative for customer-facing features; initial policy favors revert-to-stable-with-notification instead of blind rollback.
acceptance_criteria: API: create_experiment and update_traffic endpoints that accept seedable split strategy and safety_budget param
Scheduler: deterministic routing for traffic-splits (same user id -> consistent variant) with 99.9% determinism in e2e tests
Safety pipeline: signal ingestion (latency, error_rate, quality_metric) and threshold evaluation with pluggable aggregators
Auto-revert: policy engine that can revert variant automatically when configured thresholds breach and record a revert event with reason
Console: experiment summary page with live traffic split, safety budget usage, and a single-click manual revert
Docs: playbook and examples (Confluence + quickstart repo) with at least two example experiment configs
tasks: Design API schema for experiments (PM + Eng) and finalize request/response shape
Implement deterministic traffic hashing library (ENG) and add SDK helpers
Build safety signal pipeline: latency, error, and 'quality delta' collectors
Policy engine: declarative rules -> action mapping, include cooldown and manual override
Console UI: live experiment panel, safety-usage graph, and revert button
Write playbook docs, quickstart repo, and example configs
Integrate alerts to PagerDuty and internal ops channel on auto-revert events
Run 3 internal pilot experiments and capture learnings
